data.outcome_summary: This OECD report analyzes PISA 2015 science data (computer-based science assessment with multiple-choice and constructed-response items) and links it to students’ and teachers’ reports of science teaching practices. It constructs composite indices for enquiry-based science teaching, teacher-directed instruction, adaptive teaching, teacher support, and teacher feedback, using IRT scaling for student-reported indices and additional teacher-reported indices aggregated to the school level. The report then estimates associations between these teaching indices and science performance as well as multiple science-related dispositions (enjoyment, interest, epistemic beliefs, self-efficacy, and expectations of a science career), using regression approaches including fixed-effects and logistic/quantile regressions. Key results include: enquiry-based teaching’s negative association with science performance is attenuated in disciplined classrooms; teacher-directed instruction shows positive associations with science outcomes across contexts; adaptive teaching and teacher support are generally positively associated with science performance; and teacher feedback shows a negative association with science performance that weakens after accounting for student/school profiles and becomes positive once reading and mathematics performance are considered. The excerpt does not document PV handling or missing-data procedures, so uncertainty estimation for PV-based science scores cannot be verified here.
